dict.string: MacPilot needs permission to manage inactive apps.

MacPilot uses Bluetooth to detect nearby BLE devices (such as your iPhone or Apple Watch) for proximity-based screen lock and unlock, and to let your own paired iPhone reach this Mac when the two are not on the same network.
MacPilot uses Bluetooth to detect nearby BLE devices for proximity-based screen lock and unlock.
MacPilot shows the camera in a floating overlay window that is captured into screen recordings.
MacPilot uses the microphone to record narration as a separate audio track in screen recordings. Audio stays on your Mac.
MacPilot needs location access to read the connected Wi-Fi name and quit apps on the Wi-Fi networks you choose. Your location is not recorded or sent anywhere.
MacPilot reads the connected Wi-Fi name for your Wi-Fi quit rules.
MacPilot needs local network access so PilotNest can discover this nearby Mac and connect securely for remote control. Connections stay between your devices; nothing is sent to the internet.
MacPilot captures selected windows and displays for Picture-in-Picture and periodic screenshots. Captured images stay on your Mac.
